pattern.top_pattern: Unmapped facility classification is obscuring site-of-care decisions in TX and LA DSNP
pattern.what_is_impacting: TX and LA / Not Mapped facility claims / DSNP HMO
pattern.pattern_details: A meaningful share of DSNP cost movement in TX and a smaller pocket in LA is landing in a Not Mapped facility bucket. That prevents clean site-of-care, provider mix, and authorization interpretation because the claims cannot be reliably assigned to the right facility type. This needs to be fixed before the business treats the pattern as true utilization or unit-cost change.
pattern.why_it_matters: If facility mapping is wrong, site-of-care strategy and provider accountability will be misdirected.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Correct the facility mapping for Not Mapped DSNP claims in TX and LA, then rebuild the affected site-of-care and authorization reporting before taking provider or UM action.
pattern.validation_reason: The claims are explicitly concentrated in a Not Mapped facility bucket, so business interpretation is not reliable until classification is corrected.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO Not Mapped facility claims increased by about $8.5M with 214 more admissions and about $27.9K higher paid per admit.

LA DSNP HMO Not Mapped facility claims added about $283K with 23 more admissions, but paid per admit fell by about $26.8K, which is more consistent with classification noise than a stable site-of-care trend.
